source.author: ov
source.text: Natus homo est, sive hunc divino semine fecit ille opifex rerum, mundi melioris origo, sive recens tellus seductaque nuper ab alto aethere cognati retinebat semina caeli; quam satus Iapeto mixtam pluvialibus undis finxit in effigiem moderantum cuncta deorum.
source.text_original: Natus homo est, sive hunc divino semine fecit / ille opifex rerum, mundi melioris origo, / sive recens tellus seductaque nuper ab alto / aethere cognati retinebat semina caeli; / quam satus Iapeto mixtam pluvialibus undis / finxit in effigiem moderantum cuncta deorum.
source.text_english: Man was born, whether that craftsman of things, the source of a better world, made him from divine seed, or whether the newly formed earth, recently separated from the lofty air, still held the seeds of its kindred heaven; and the son of Iapetus, mingling it with rainwater, shaped it into the likeness of the gods who govern all things.

reuse.author: lact
reuse.text: quae utique omnia non Iuppiter fecit, ante annos mille septingentos natus est, sed ille opifex rerum, mundi melioris origo, qui deus, cuius principium quoniam non potest comprehendi, ne quaeri quidem debet.
reuse.text_original: quae utique omnia non Iuppiter fecit, ante annos mille septingentos natus est, sed ille opifex rerum, mundi melioris origo, qui deus, cuius principium quoniam non potest comprehendi, ne quaeri quidem debet.
reuse.text_english: All these things, of course, were not made by Jupiter, since he was born only seventeen hundred years ago, but by that maker of all things, the source of a better world, who is God, whose beginning, since it cannot be grasped, ought not even to be sought.
